Apex Industrial Corp. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Industrial Corp. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. If you're using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the STAR key. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Industrial Corp.'s results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Mark Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking in nature and subject to certain risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Mark Reynolds.

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report on Apex Industrial Corp.'s performance for the third quarter. We've made significant progress on several fronts, and I'd like to highlight a few key achievements. First, our automation and digital offerings continued to accelerate, delivering strong revenue growth and meaningful efficiency gains for our customers across manufacturing operations. Second, we've seen notable improvements in supply chain constraints and component availability, with lead times compressing and inventories building strategically. Third, our backlog reached record levels, providing excellent revenue visibility. Fourth, the book-to-bill ratio strengthened, reflecting robust demand trends. Fifth, we've gained market share in several key regions and segments through innovative solutions. And sixth, total order intake grew impressively year-over-year, underscoring end-market strength.

We are confident that our strategic initiatives are positioning us for long-term sustainable growth.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Lisa Chen to provide more detail on our financial results.

Lisa Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Mark. Turning to our financial performance, Apex Industrial Corp. reported $1.62 billion in revenue for the quarter, representing a 12% increase year-over-year. Gross margin expanded to 36.5%, driven by a favorable mix shift toward high-margin digital solutions, pricing discipline, and operational efficiencies from our manufacturing footprint. Operating expenses were $520 million, reflecting targeted investments in R&D and supply chain resilience, resulting in an operating income of $380 million. Our net income for the quarter was $280 million, or $1.85 per diluted share.

We are managing our capital allocation effectively, prioritizing investments in high-growth areas like automation and electrification while returning capital to shareholders through $75 million in share repurchases and a quarterly dividend.

Before moving to operations, let me expand on those key achievements Mark highlighted, as they provide critical context for our results and outlook in the manufacturing and industrial equipment sector.

Starting with our automation and digital offerings, this remains one of our brightest growth areas, transforming operational efficiency for customers amid labor shortages, supply volatility, and the shift to smart manufacturing. Our Automation and Digital segment generated $452 million in revenue, up 28% year-over-year, now comprising 35% of our total revenue mix compared to 28% last year. Pure digital revenue—including cloud-based IIoT platforms, AI analytics, and subscription services—jumped 45% to $128 million, with annual recurring revenue reaching $512 million, a 52% rise. This high-margin stream, at 68% gross margins versus 42% for traditional hardware, drove a 320 basis point expansion in segment EBITDA margins to 29%.

These solutions are delivering real efficiency impacts. For instance, our platforms have boosted customers' overall equipment effectiveness, or OEE, by an average 18%, lifting typical discrete manufacturing plants from 65-70% to over 85%. Predictive maintenance, leveraging machine learning on 15 petabytes of shop-floor data, cuts downtime by 32% and improves energy efficiency by 22% via optimized controls and variable frequency drives. We've backed this with our Efficiency Guarantee program, issuing $14 million in rebates this year for underperformance.

Key drivers include IndustroEdge AI, our edge-computing platform in PLCs and HMIs, with over 45,000 nodes shipped this quarter—up 60%—enabling 40% faster changeovers for automotive suppliers. Our Digital Twin Suite, using advanced simulation tech, supports 65% of new greenfield projects, cutting prototyping costs by 50% and production timelines by 3-4 months, especially in EV battery plants. And IndustroConnect, our MES-SCADA platform with ERP integrations, powers 75% of digital ARR growth through real-time scheduling and generative AI anomaly detection, slashing false positives by 55%.

Regionally, APAC led with 42% of sales and 38% growth, boosted by initiatives like Made in China 2025 and India's PLI scheme, including a $150 million cobot deal in electronics. EMEA grew 25% to 30% of sales, driven by EU Green Deal retrofits yielding 28% energy savings. The Americas rose 22%, with strong automotive and mining uptake reducing scrap by 25% and boosting uptime by 35%.

We're investing $250 million from free cash flow into R&D, including a $100 million acquisition for autonomous mobile robots, targeting a digital mix of 45% by FY25 and consolidated EBITDA margins of 24%. With a book-to-bill of 1.35:1 and $2.1 billion backlog, we're well-insulated amid rebounding CAPEX.

Next, on supply chain constraints and component availability, we've made meaningful strides. Critical lead times fell 28% quarter-over-quarter to 16 weeks from 22, nearing pre-pandemic levels, with tier-one inventory at 145 days of coverage. Semiconductors, 18% of BOM, improved 35% via dual-sourcing from TSMC and Samsung facilities. Mechanical components like bearings and cylinders dropped 22% to 12 weeks through long-term contracts with SKF and Timken, while our Mexico facility localizes 40% of rare earth magnets.

North America shipped 92% on time, Europe pivoted to air freight minimizing costs, and APAC benefited from Vietnam/India diversification. AI demand sensing hit 92% accuracy, supplier scorecards diversified our base to 250 vendors, and $45 million capex targets titanium additive manufacturing for further gains. This rebounded gross margins to 34.2%, with $2.8 billion backlog up 14% YoY and only 8% order pushouts.

Turning to backlog value, it hit $3.4 billion at quarter-end, up 28% year-over-year and 12% sequentially—our highest in five years. Book-to-bill was 1.35x, above peers. By end-market: Aerospace & Defense at 42% or $1.43 billion, up 35%; Automotive & EV 28% or $952 million, up 22%; Energy Transition 20% or $680 million, up 40%; General Industrial 10% or $340 million. Regionally: North America 52% or $1.77 billion, up 32%; EMEA 26% or $884 million, up 18%; APAC 18% or $612 million, up 25%.

Visibility is strong: 68% converts in 12 months, 45% in 6 months, aided by digital twins cutting cycles 18%, capacity expansions, and 4-6% price escalators. This supports low double-digit growth.

On book-to-bill trends, we achieved 1.18x for the quarter, up from 1.10x prior and 0.92x last year, with TTM at 1.12x—strongest since 2021. By segment: A&D 1.25x, Semis 1.35x, Automotive 1.05x, Energy 1.15x. Regions: North America 1.22x, APAC 1.28x, EMEA 1.08x. Drivers include supply normalization, 92% capacity utilization, and Industry 4.0 in 85% of orders lifting ASPs 12%. Backlog at $12.4 billion provides 14 months visibility; expect 1.15-1.25x ongoing.

Market share expanded 180 bps to 13.8% globally. North America up 250 bps to 18.2% in CNC; Europe +90 bps to 12.4%, gaining in robotics; APAC flat at 9.6% but +4.2 points in premium automation; emerging +2.1 points. R&D at 8.2% of sales fuels this, targeting 15%+ share in FY24.

Finally, total order intake was $1.28 billion, +18% YoY, ninth straight double-digit quarter. TTM $4.95 billion, +16%, book-to-bill 1.25x. Segments: Heavy Machinery $665M +21%, Automation $358M +25%, Precision $257M +8%. Regions: Americas $538M +24%, EMEA $397M +12%, APAC $345M +15%. TechStack 3.0 shortens delivery, pipeline up 30%.

These metrics reinforce our FY24 guidance. I'll hand over to David for operations.

David Patel (COO):
Thank you, Lisa. Operationally, we've focused on productivity and efficiency across our facilities. Lean principles and data analytics have optimized processes, while new technologies bolster supply chain resilience, aligning with Lisa's updates on lead times and inventory. Capacity utilization hit 92%, and expansions like our Dayton fab support backlog conversion. We're addressing labor dynamics through training, tying into our digital tools that reduce reliance on manual oversight.

Now to Elena for our technology roadmap.

Elena Vasquez (CTO):
Thank you, David. We're driving innovation with heavy R&D in AI, machine learning, and IoT. Our new Digital Twin Suite and IndustroEdge AI are delivering early wins, with OEE uplifts and downtime cuts as Lisa detailed. The autonomous mobile robots acquisition enhances our stack, positioning us to transform industrial operations against platforms like FactoryTalk or Ability. These create outsized opportunities as digital scales to 45% of revenue.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press STAR then 1 on your touchtone phone. Our first question comes from John Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

John Carter (Morgan Stanley):
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the growth drivers in your digital solutions business?

Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, John. Absolutely—our digital solutions are surging due to the tangible efficiency gains they're unlocking. As Lisa noted, pure digital revenue grew 45% to $128 million, with ARR at $512 million. Flagship products like IndustroEdge AI, with 45,000 nodes shipped, and Digital Twin Suite in 65% of greenfields are key. IndustroConnect drives 75% of ARR via closed-loop optimization. Regionally, APAC's 38% growth from cobots, EMEA's Green Deal retrofits, and Americas' reshoring all contribute. With $250 million R&D, including AMRs, we're projecting mid-20s% growth, expanding margins as scale kicks in.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Maria Lopez (Goldman Sachs):
What are your plans for expanding your presence in emerging markets?

Mark Reynolds:
Good question, Maria. Emerging markets are a priority, building on our gains—India up 410 bps to 11.3% share via localized Pune production, Latin America's +2.1 points in agribusiness. APAC at 27% of intake grew 15%, with India rail orders +50%. We're leveraging PLI schemes, nearshoring in Mexico/Vietnam covering 30% castings, and JVs for electrified drives. Capacity in Poland/Mexico supports this without margin dilution, targeting double-digit growth amid commodity cycles and infrastructure pipelines.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly (JPMorgan):
How are you addressing the skilled labor shortage in the manufacturing sector?

David Patel:
Thanks, Tom. Labor shortages are industry-wide, but our digital automation mitigates this effectively. Solutions like AI-optimized recipe management cut changeovers 40%, cobots handle high-mix tasks with 25% cycle reductions, and predictive tools boost OEE 18%, reducing headcount needs. Workforce programs invest in upskilling for Industry 4.0, while digital twins slash prototyping time. ROI under 12 months in rising-cost regions like APAC helps clients. Our 92% utilization and supplier diversification keep us agile.

Operator:
Thank you. There are no further questions at this time.

Mark Reynolds (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Industrial Corp. We are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, everyone, for joining us today. This concludes our earnings call. Have a great day.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.
